name: Offerlume Offerwall Rewards
author: Sipho Nhlapo

sections.description:
Offerlume creates a landing page, dashboard, offerwall directory, history, referrals, withdrawal, terms, privacy, contact, registration, sign-in and password reset pages. Its own responsive template replaces the theme header and footer on these pages. Public pages do not show the member sidebar. WordPress stores the member accounts.

Site administrators can edit landing sections, FAQ, page labels and other portal text under Offerwall Rewards > Page content. Terms, privacy and other page content can be edited in the WordPress page editor. The site operator must replace the starter legal text with their actual policies before launch. No faucet, PTC or shortlinks are included.

A directory lists 19 optional networks, including CPX Research, Prime Earn, TimeWall, TheoremReach, BitLabs, Lootably, Notik, GemiAd, Monlix, ayeT Studios, Easy Surveys, Offerwall, Wannads, Pollfish, AdGate Media, Torox, RevU, inBrain and TapResearch. Names are optional setup choices, not endorsements or promises of approval. All networks start disabled. Administrators must obtain their own publisher agreements and verify that the network permits their incentivized traffic and redemption model.

BitLabs has a built-in signed callback. Other networks require separate server-side adapters that authenticate the actual network callback and send a signed normalized event to the plugin. Merely entering an offerwall URL and adapter secret cannot credit rewards. The provider setup screen links to publisher sites and available documentation. BitLabs signed debug callbacks confirm delivery without crediting points. Test actual conversions and reversals on staging before opening a network to members.

Members earn integer points only from confirmed callbacks and may receive referral bonuses. They can request manual payouts using methods enabled by the site operator, such as PayPal, Stripe Connect, crypto wallet, NOWPayments, bank transfer, FaucetPay, Skrill or Wise. The plugin reserves points and records payout status; it does not send money, call payout APIs or guarantee a cash value. The operator must settle each approved request externally and enter a real transaction reference.

External services and privacy

The plugin makes no external requests merely on activation or when browsing its pages. Opening an enabled offerwall sends the member’s numeric WordPress user ID in the administrator-configured external URL so the provider can attribute the offer. The network may collect additional device, offer, survey and activity data under its own policies. The plugin does not share the member email address with a network. Site administrators choose which networks to enable and must disclose their active providers, policies, retention, user rights and payout arrangements on their site’s own legal pages. Provider publisher signup and documentation links on the admin screen open only when an administrator clicks them.

BitLabs (the built-in integration) provides an offerwall and signed reward/reconciliation callbacks. A member’s numeric ID is sent when that member opens the BitLabs offerwall. BitLabs publisher terms: https://dashboard.bitlabs.ai/termsOfService ; BitLabs user privacy policy: https://bitlabs.ai/offerwall-privacy-policy . Integration documentation: https://developer.bitlabs.ai/docs/general-reward-callbacks . The site owner must read and comply with its current publisher agreement.

For other networks, the plugin supplies optional listings and a generic adapter endpoint only; no native network integration is bundled. The site administrator supplies the external provider URL, must document that provider’s current terms and privacy policy on the site’s pages, and must create or obtain an adapter that verifies the network signature before sending a normalized event. No data is sent to any disabled network. Enabling a network is a deliberate site-administrator setting, and its provider receives a numeric member ID only when the member opens its wall. Payment providers are not called by the plugin; payment destinations and references stay in WordPress until the operator handles a payout externally.

Locally stored data includes account IDs, referral relationships, conversion records, point balances, payout destinations and settlement references. The plugin registers a suggested WordPress privacy policy notice and personal-data export and erase callbacks; financial audit records are retained while completed payout destinations can be cleared. The site owner sets an appropriate retention period and handles legal requests. The plugin does not automatically remove database records when deactivated.

Callback security and testing

For BitLabs, configure the signed GET callback URL and parameter order shown in Offerwall Rewards settings. The plugin verifies the HMAC-SHA1 signature of the exact callback URL before processing a conversion. The BitLabs dashboard Callback Tester sends debug=true: valid signed debug requests are acknowledged and their receipt time shown in Provider setup, without creating points or reversing balances. A real allowed conversion on staging is required to test crediting. Full negative reconciliations with the original reference can reverse points; partial adjustments need manual review.

Other networks must call a trusted adapter, not the generic endpoint. The adapter verifies the native provider signature, maps eligible rewards to whole-number site points, ignores pending/sandbox events and POSTs JSON to /wp-json/offerlume/v1/callback/{provider}. Required fields: user_id (integer), transaction_id (unique ID), amount (positive integer points), status (approved or reversed), signature (hex HMAC-SHA256). Sign provider|user_id|transaction_id|amount|status with that provider’s adapter secret. Reversals use the original transaction ID, member ID and positive amount. The plugin deduplicates events. A URL or generic test POST alone does not prove that a provider integration works.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the ZIP under Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, then activate. If you have the earlier offerlume-offerwall folder installed, deactivate it first, upload and activate this package under offerlume-offerwall-rewards, and only then delete the inactive old plugin. Its existing rewards settings and data are retained. Purge any full-page cache after switching.
  2. Edit the created terms and privacy pages. Set the points-to-currency estimate, minimum payout, referral rate and payout methods. Choose the rewards landing page as the site homepage only if wanted.
  3. Under Offerwall Rewards > Provider setup, follow the relevant network’s publisher instructions and confirm your site is approved. BitLabs needs an App/API Token, App Secret and signed callback configuration. Other networks need a trusted adapter and a real HTTPS URL containing {user_id}.
  4. On staging, check registration, password reset and email delivery. Use the provider’s approved testing tools where available, and verify a permitted real conversion, duplicate retry and reversal. Never put shared callback secrets in browser code.
sections.faq:
Do listed networks work immediately?

No. BitLabs must be configured and approved. All other networks also require a network-specific authenticated server adapter. Provider signup and test instructions are shown in the admin area, where public documentation exists.

Are payouts automatic?

No. The administrator pays outside WordPress and records the result. Points are internal accounting units, not cryptocurrency.

Can I edit the pages?

Yes. Portal labels and landing text are in Page content. Legal text and extra page blocks can be edited in the WordPress page editor.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Added standalone public and member layouts, landing sections, registration and password reset, editable content and manual payout methods.
  • Added verified BitLabs callbacks, provider setup links and signed debug-test receipt without balance changes.
  • Added provider adapter contract, referral rewards, reward history and withdrawal review.
  • Used prepared database identifiers and escaped admin nonce fields for WordPress plugin review.

1.0.0

  • Initial offerwall rewards portal with optional network directory, referrals and point ledger.
